claim_support.claim: Variational quantum algorithms train parameterized circuits with classical optimizers and face trainability, accuracy, and efficiency challenges.
claim_support.evidence: The publisher abstract defines VQAs and names these three challenges.

claim_support.claim: Fair quantum-machine-learning comparisons require explicit classical baselines, hyperparameter treatment, and reproducible experimental settings.
claim_support.evidence: The article compares quantum and classical models with randomized hyperparameter search and emphasizes transparent quantum configuration choices.

claim_support.claim: Quantum classifiers tuned by hyperparameter search still trail modern boosting methods.
claim_support.evidence: Abstract: VQC and QKE outperform Ridge and Lasso but do not match the accuracy and runtime of XGBoost, LightGBM or CatBoost; QML currently lags behind classical approaches.

claim_support.claim: Hybrid transfer learning can use a pretrained classical network to extract image features for a final variational quantum circuit.
claim_support.evidence: The journal abstract explicitly describes this paradigm and image-recognition demonstrations.

claim_support.claim: Channel attention has been proposed for quantum convolutional neural networks in quantum phase classification.
claim_support.evidence: The article abstract introduces QCNN channel attention and evaluates quantum phase classification.

claim_support.claim: Data re-uploading repeatedly interleaves input encoding and trainable circuit processing to construct expressive quantum classifiers.
claim_support.evidence: The journal abstract describes a sequence of data re-uploading and single-qubit processing units.

claim_support.claim: Deep convolutional models can recognize isolated static sign-language gestures.
claim_support.evidence: The article presents and evaluates deep convolutional models for static sign-language recognition.

claim_support.claim: Signer-specific representations can hinder generalization to unseen signers, motivating explicit signer-independent evaluation.
claim_support.evidence: The article abstract identifies signer dependence as a generalization problem and evaluates signer-independent representation learning.

claim_support.claim: Deep-learning surveys of sign language recognition cover a range of vision-based models and note variability in hand shape, motion, and body pose.
claim_support.evidence: The abstract reviews vision-based sign-language recognition models from recent years and names variability in hand shape, motion profile, and body position.

claim_support.claim: Quanvolutional layers transform local image patches with quantum circuits before a classical network continues the recognition pipeline.
claim_support.evidence: The abstract introduces a quanvolutional layer that locally transforms input data with random quantum circuits, analogously to convolution.

claim_support.claim: SE recalibrates channels with a two-layer bottleneck on pooled features; the TPAMI article is the archival version of SE.
claim_support.evidence: Journal version of Squeeze-and-Excitation Networks describing squeeze (global pooling) and excitation (bottleneck FC + sigmoid).

claim_support.claim: DenseNet121 is the densely connected convolutional backbone used for feature extraction.
claim_support.evidence: TPAMI journal version of DenseNet presenting dense connectivity architectures including DenseNet-121.

claim_support.claim: Barren plateaus depend on cost-function locality and system size in shallow parametrised circuits.
claim_support.evidence: Title and abstract establish cost-function-dependent barren plateaus.

claim_support.claim: The data-encoding strategy determines the frequency spectrum accessible to a variational quantum model.
claim_support.evidence: Abstract shows that variational models are partial Fourier series whose frequencies are fixed by the encoding gates; repetition enlarges the spectrum.

claim_support.claim: Variational algorithms are the main approach on NISQ devices, and hardware noise constrains them.
claim_support.evidence: Review of NISQ algorithms centred on variational methods and noise.

claim_support.claim: Quantum convolutional networks have been applied to classical data after classical dimensionality reduction.
claim_support.evidence: Abstract benchmarks QCNN on MNIST/Fashion-MNIST with classical reduction.

claim_support.claim: Classical learners with access to data can match quantum models on many tasks.
claim_support.evidence: Abstract: classical ML models trained on data can be competitive with quantum models; proposes projected quantum kernels.

claim_support.claim: Transformers have been used for joint continuous sign language recognition and translation.
claim_support.evidence: Title and abstract.

claim_support.claim: Effective dimension relates model capacity to trainable parameters for quantum neural networks.
claim_support.evidence: Abstract introduces effective dimension as capacity measure for QNNs; the measure is bounded by parameter count by construction.

claim_support.claim: Generalisation error of QML models is bounded in terms of the number of trainable gates.
claim_support.evidence: Abstract: generalisation error scales as sqrt(T/N) for T trainable gates and N training points.

claim_support.claim: Quantum ML research should look beyond chasing quantum-advantage claims.
claim_support.evidence: Perspective argues advantage is not the right sole goal.

claim_support.claim: Hardware noise can induce barren plateaus and flatten the training landscape.
claim_support.evidence: Title and abstract.

claim_support.claim: ECA replaces the SE bottleneck with a local 1D convolution and achieves comparable or better accuracy with far fewer parameters.
claim_support.evidence: Abstract reports efficient channel attention with few parameters and performance gains over SE-style counterparts.

claim_support.claim: Survey of attention mechanisms, including channel attention, in computer vision.
claim_support.evidence: Survey title and taxonomy include channel attention (SE, ECA).

claim_support.claim: Hybrid quantum-classical convolutional networks place trainable circuits inside classical CNN pipelines.
claim_support.evidence: Title and abstract.

claim_support.claim: CNNs reach about 99.98% accuracy on the 87,000-image Kaggle ASL Alphabet set.
claim_support.evidence: Abstract: ResNet-50 99.98% on over 87,000 ASL alphabet images; AlexNet, ConvNeXt, EfficientNet, ViT compared.

claim_support.claim: Recent hybrid quantum-classical-quantum CNN designs for image classification.
claim_support.evidence: Title and abstract.

claim_support.claim: Data sampling and initialisation produce benchmark variance that can change method rankings.
claim_support.evidence: Abstract: variance due to data sampling, parameter initialisation, and hyperparameters markedly impacts ML benchmarks.

claim_support.claim: Static hand gestures on the Massey University (MU) ASL dataset have been evaluated with leave-one-subject-out validation; signer independence matters for real use.
claim_support.evidence: Abstract: fine-tuned CNN with score fusion evaluated with leave-one-subject-out CV on two benchmark static hand gesture datasets (the full text names the Massey University dataset); aims at a user-independent interface.
